race_context: The district: Lakeland School Corporation is based in LaGrange. It serves Lima, Greenfield, Bloomfield and Johnson townships and part of Clay Township in LaGrange County, including the town of Wolcottville, which reaches into Noble County {lk_bm}. Its schools are Lakeland Primary, Lakeland Intermediate and Lakeland Jr./Sr. High School {kpc_profile}. The superintendent's enrollment counts fell from 1,446 in February 2025 to 1,395 in June 2026 {lk_min250212}{lk_min260610}. Dr. Traci Blaize has been superintendent since October 2022, and on June 10, 2026 the board approved her contract 6-0 {kpc_blaize}{lk_min260610}.

Board: six members, each assigned to a geographic district. District 1 is Greenfield Township, District 2 is Lima Township, District 3 is Bloomfield Township outside the town of LaGrange, District 4 is the town of LaGrange and part of Clay Township (two members), and District 5 is Johnson Township, including Wolcottville {lk_board}. In January 2026 the board re-elected Brett Bateman president, Derrick Sherck vice president and Rob West secretary; the other members are Sue Keenan, Kara Howard and Shelley Gould {lk_min260114r}. The state list places all three 2026 races on ballots in both LaGrange and Noble counties {in_list}. That suggests voters across the district vote for each seat, but no fetched source states the voting method directly.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three seats, one per race, matching the state list's "vote for 1" {in_list}{lgc_guide}. District 1: held by board president Brett Bateman, whose term ends in December 2026 {lk_board}. He is not on the ballot; Kari Cossairt and Charles (Bill) Park are running {in_list}. District 2: held by Kara Howard, whose term ends in December 2026 {lk_board}. She is not on the ballot; Robert Bond is unopposed {in_list}. District 4: one of its two seats is held by board secretary Rob West, whose term ends in December 2026 {lk_board}. He is not on the ballot; Ben Brown is unopposed {in_list}. The other District 4 member, Sue Keenan, serves until 2028 {lk_board}. No fetched source explains why the three incumbents did not file.

Party labels: on the state list, Charles (Bill) Park, Robert Bond and Ben Brown are Republican, and Kari Cossairt is Nonpartisan {in_list}. The LaGrange County Chamber of Commerce voter guide shows the same labels {lgc_guide}.

Enrollment and building sale: in February 2025 Blaize said the district expected enrollment to drop over the next three years because graduating classes are larger than kindergarten classes, and was preparing for smaller education fund revenue {kpc_lima}. The district accepted an offer from Great Commission University (part of World Olivet Assembly) for the former Lima-Brighton Elementary in Howe, which had closed in 2019 along with Wolcott Mills Elementary {kpc_lima}. Blaize said the sale would help "position LSC to excel in our infrastructure, staff pay and curriculum expansions" {kpc_lima}. The board voted 5-0 on Dec. 10, 2025 to approve a Lima building sale resolution {lk_min251210}. On Aug. 12, 2026 it voted 5-0 on a resolution to transfer real estate {lk_min260812}.

Facilities and bonds: in September 2025 the district announced two bonds. One covers a new cafeteria, an office addition with a secure entrance and an auditorium renovation at the Jr./Sr. High. The other covers Lakeland Primary updates and a secure entrance, a partial roof and playground at Wolcott Mills, and a new maintenance building {kpc_bonds25}. The district said it has the seventh-lowest debt service rate of all Indiana schools {kpc_bonds25}. At the Sept. 2025 project hearing, the board approved the Jr./Sr. High project 6-0 and the Wolcott Mills/Lakeland Primary project 5-1 {lk_min250910h}. The minutes do not say who voted no {lk_min250910h}. In June 2026 the board gave notice of two more financings: up to $3,150,000 in general obligation bonds for roofing, HVAC, athletics and other improvements, and $6,865,000 in lease-backed bonds mainly for Lakeland Intermediate (safety, HVAC and roofing) {lk_gob}{lk_lease}. The board held a lease and bond hearing on July 8, 2026 {lk_lease_hr}.

Budget: the board adopted the 2026 budget 5-0 on Oct. 22, 2025, along with tax-rate, capital projects and bus replacement resolutions {lk_min251022}. No fetched minutes or news describe how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Lakeland.

Safety and curriculum: in February 2025 parents raised concerns about aggressive student behavior in first-grade classrooms and about how students are removed from classrooms {lk_min250212}. In August 2026 the board approved a school resource officer agreement 5-0 {lk_min260812}. On May 13, 2026 it approved new K-8 mathematics curriculum and a human sexuality curriculum, each 6-0 {lk_min260513}. In 2026 the minutes refer to a combined "Lakeland Elementary School" handbook, and on Aug. 12, 2026 the board approved a school name change 5-0 {lk_min260610}{lk_min260812}. The minutes do not name the school.

Board meetings: 2025-26 minutes record few public comments and mostly unanimous votes {lk_min251210}{lk_min260610}{lk_min260909}. On June 10, 2026 the athletic handbook and the high-ability handbook each passed 5-1 {lk_min260610}.

Forums: the LaGrange County Chamber of Commerce scheduled a "Connect With The Candidates" event for Oct. 20, 2026 at Lakeland Intermediate School, after this profile's review date {lgc_guide}{kpc_letter}. No news coverage, questionnaire or campaign statement from any of the four Lakeland candidates was found.
